thread.title: Stock Indexes Take Wait-And-See Stance, But Some Leaders Pop

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: Stock Indexes Take Wait-And-See Stance, But Some Leaders Pop
text:
U.S. stock indexes were mixed near midday Friday, as Canada and the White House tried to reach an agreement on trade. In the meantime, there has been no trade progress vis-à-vis China.
X The Nasdaq inched up 0.1%, while the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones industrial average lost 0.1% and 0.2%, respectively. Small caps were quiet with the S&P 600 up less than 0.1%.
Volume fell on both major exchanges. The stock market's modest gains in slow turnover suggested funds were taking a wait-and-see attitude.
Trade appeared to be the main catalyst behind the caution.

Please contact customer service CLOSE President Trump is pushing for Canada's inclusion in the trade pact with Mexico. The Washington Post reported that Congress is unlikely to approve the agreement unless both Canada and Mexico are included. Trump will need the approval of Congress.
Canada's top trade negotiator Chrystia Freeland said Thursday that talks had turned intense. There was no progress reported early Friday.
Meanwhile, Reuters reported a comic turn in China's trade struggles vs. Trump. Ordinary Chinese citizens have turned to fortune-tellers to figure out what's likely to happen.
The U.S. stock market probably could've used a fortune-teller for this year's market. The market has advanced, but action has been sloppy. The Nasdaq has dropped to near the 200-day area three times, in February, March and April. Since then the market has come down to the 50-day line three times, in June, July and August. But new highs were scored in January, March, June, July and August.
Stocks On The Move On Friday, Apple ( AAPL ) led the Dow with a 1.2% gain. Ulta Beauty ( ULTA ) paced the large cap S&P 500 with an 8% gain. Firearms maker Sturm Ruger ( RGR ) was near the top of the small cap S&P 600 with a 5% pop.
In the IBD 50, which is a list of the top stocks in fundamentals and technicals, chip designer Integrated Device Technology ( IDTI ) gapped up 11% in terrific volume on reports of a possible merger with Japan's Renesas.
Apparel retailer Lululemon Athletica ( LULU ), another IBD 50 stock, jumped 15% after reporting strong results late Thursday.
